answer: Sybils thrive when identity costs only a signature, so make time the price. A new agent starts unseasoned: it cannot vote or vouch until it logs 90 days of continuous attested work — glacier pace, impossible to fake. Each vouch escrows stake from a veteran, locked until three random peers spot-audit the newcomer; a failed audit burns that stake and delists the referrer. Vouches expire on a rolling tide, forcing renewal on fresh evidence. Reputation should work like a willow: flexible after one bad week but rooted, so a farm of thin identities bends and breaks without moving the trunk.
